transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood PM); Michael Ortega (Gamma CTO), Sara Li (PM), Devon Park (ML Eng), Anjali Rao (Security)

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on structured output / JSON mode and function-calling for Gamma's automation use-case; reviewed guardrails, schema-binding, console demos, cost/latency tradeoffs, and next steps for a bench/poc.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm here with Priya our SE and Jordan, who's product. thanks for making time. Michael, do you want to kick off with a one line of what you're hoping to see?

[00:18] Michael Ortega: Yeah thanks Alex, uh main thing is we want a reliable way to generate structured order updates and routing metadata from messy customer emails. We're evaluating structured output + function calling; primary constraints are latency < 500ms p50 for simple ops, strong guardrails to avoid hallucinations, and data residency / KMS for keys.

[00:40] Alex Chen: Great, makes sense. Priya i'm going to hand it over to you for the demo but quick question — are you leaning hosted or thinking about Dedicated right away?

[00:52] Michael Ortega: We want to start hosted for speed but need to validate SLA and security; if traffic ramps we might want Dedicated or private.

[01:05] Priya Nair: Cool, i'll share my screen — demo is focused on JSON mode structured output with schema validation, and function-calling to webhook / internal functions. i'll show the API call, Console view, and Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.

[01:28] [screen share noise] Priya Nair: ok first example — simple prompt that asks the model to extract order_id, customer_name, issue_type, priority, and suggested_routing. you can see here i attach a JSON schema in the request body: type: object, required: [order_id, issue_type], properties...

[01:52] Devon Park: quick q — does the schema run locally in the runtime or is it a post-hoc validator? we need deterministic behaviour.

[02:05] Priya Nair: good question. Redwood's JSON mode enforces schema constraints at generation time using structured sampling heuristics plus a post-generation validator; if the output doesn't match the schema we can auto-retry with a temperature reduction or fallback to a strict parser mode. so you get deterministic rejections vs silent bad JSON.

[02:32] Sara Li: can it call internal functions? e.g., if the model extracts suggested_routing = "refund", can it then call our routing API?

[02:40] Priya Nair: absolutely — function calling is first-class. you register a function signature (name, args schema, destination webhook or lambda) and the runtime will output a call intent that we translate into a function invocation. we also support pre-configured guardrails to ensure only allowed functions are called.

[03:05] Anjali Rao: security — how do we protect secrets in that flow? KMS? HSM? logs?

[03:13] Jordan Kim: we integrate with customer KMS for key material, and logs can be redacted or routed to customer-only S3. in Private/Dedicated we can isolate the control plane; audit logs include token-level traces but we can redact sensitive fields. we'll send our security whitepaper after this call.

[03:40] [priYa stumbles on spelling] Priya Nair: okay switching to live API call. here's a cURL to /v1/generate with content-type application/json, include schema and function schema. temperature 0.0 for extraction.

[04:02] [console clicks] Priya Nair: note the "strict_json": true flag — that'll enforce exact field types. i'm going to run against a small example email.

[04:20] [run delay, console showing tokens]

[04:35] Priya Nair: ok output came back — you can see it returned a function_call object with name: route_ticket and arguments that match the schema. the JSON is valid and we show a preview in Console with color-coded validation state.

[04:55] Michael Ortega: nice — what's the typical latency for that round trip? including function invocation?

[05:03] Priya Nair: for a short extraction and internal webhook it's usually 150–350ms p50 on hosted with our optimized kernels. that includes generation and a small sync call. if you need sub-100ms we'd talk Dedicated sizing and model selection.

[05:25] Devon Park: any token-cost differences when using JSON mode and function calling? we care about unit economics.

[05:33] Alex Chen: JSON mode might cost slightly more because we bias sampling and sometimes emit longer structured text, but Redwood Optimize suggests batching and caching opportunities — e.g., prefix caching if multiple requests share the same customer preamble — and it quantifies per-token cost impact. we'll also show recommendations for model variants that hit your latency/cost sweet spot.

[06:00] Priya Nair: switching to the Console's Structured Output panel — shows schema, recent failures, examples, and guardrail configs. you can set a hard reject, auto-retry, or fallback to a deterministic parser. here's the guardrail rules: no external PII exfiltration, function-call whitelists, regex checks for order_id format.

[06:25] Sara Li: Can we chain functions? like extract -> normalize -> call routing?

[06:33] Priya Nair: yes, we support sequential function calls; the runtime maintains a KV cache for intermediate state and you can orchestrate a pipeline either in the model (function_call returns payload triggering next function) or in the host after validation. we usually recommend keeping heavy transformations in your code-path, light parsing in the model.

[06:56] [crosstalk] Michael Ortega: what's failure behaviour if the model returns invalid JSON multiple times?

[07:05] Priya Nair: you can set retry policies: reduce temperature, increase constraints, or escalate to a fallback parser. there's also a canary route that sends suspicious outputs to a manual review queue in Console.

[07:25] Anjali Rao: audit logs — we need per-request traces for audit, and retention for 1 year. do you support that?

[07:33] Jordan Kim: yes, audit logs are configurable; retention is part of an add-on. for hosted we can provide compressed traces, for Dedicated/Private you can keep full raw traces in your VPC or S3.

[07:52] [Priya: demonstrates Optimize tab] Priya Nair: now Optimize — this suggests batching window of 20–30ms to hit cost targets while staying under your latency SLO. for your workload (mostly short extracts) Optimize recommends a small model with 4-bit quantization on a pinned instance type to keep p50 low.

[08:20] Devon Park: 4-bit quantization — any quality regression concerns when extracting structured fields?

[08:28] Priya Nair: for extraction tasks it's usually safe; Optimize runs evals on your prompt set to report extraction accuracy delta. we can run that eval for you on your sample prompts.

[08:45] Michael Ortega: about guardrails — can we enforce business logic like "if issue_type == chargeback then priority = high" as a schema-level rule?

[08:55] Priya Nair: yes, we support post-validation hooks and rule sets in Console; those can transform or reject outputs before function-calling. rules are expressible in a small DSL, and you can implement more complex checks in your post-processor.

[09:20] Alex Chen: i'm going to show function-calling to an external webhook — i'll flip to a simulated webhook so you can see the activation.

[09:32] [demo webhook traffic] Priya Nair: call succeeded; logs show request payload and redacted fields per the security config.

[09:45] Sara Li: will the webhook credentials be stored in Redwood? we prefer KMS + no-plain-text storage.

[09:53] Jordan Kim: credentials are stored encrypted with customer KMS; for Private deployments we can disable storage and require ephemeral tokens. we'll note that in the security doc.

[10:10] [small pause] Michael Ortega: timeline wise — we need a POC by mid-Jan if possible, stakeholders include infra, security, and ML.

[10:20] Alex Chen: reasonable — we usually do a 2–3 week bench to validate accuracy and latency, then a pilot. Priya will scope required assets.

[10:34] Priya Nair: i'll need sample emails, expected canonical outputs, and an API spec for routing. with those we'll run an eval and return precision/recall and latency numbers.

[10:50] Devon Park: do you support offline/on-prem for air-gapped environments? some of our customers require that.

[10:58] Jordan Kim: yes, Redwood Private is available for on-prem or VPC with an optional offline package; it includes a customer-controlled control plane and local KMS integration.

[11:15] Michael Ortega: any gotchas with rate limiting when we burst? we expect spiky loads.

[11:22] Alex Chen: we support burst capacity and autoscaling; for Dedicated you can provision burst pools. Optimize can also smooth bursts by batching and backpressure.

[11:40] [demo: Console - Failure dashboard] Priya Nair: here's a failure example where the model returned an unknown enum. Console flags it and suggests a fix — either tighten schema or add an enum mapping rule.

[12:00] Sara Li: curious about monitoring — do you expose per-route histograms and token-cost breakdowns?

[12:07] Jordan Kim: yes, Redwood Console shows per-route latency P50/P95, per-token cost, and tracing that ties outputs back to prompts, useful for regression alerts.

[12:25] Devon Park: for the evals — do you run them on our data in hosted? we have privacy concerns.

[12:33] Priya Nair: we can run evals in a few ways: on hosted with data redaction, in a dedicated ephemeral environment, or on your premises with Private. we recommend the dedicated bench for sensitive data.

[12:50] [background noise] Alex Chen: quick question — do we have any specific SLA asks?

[12:57] Michael Ortega: 99.9% uptime, p95 < 800ms for our expected load, and SOC2 compliance.

[13:10] Jordan Kim: that's in-line with our Dedicated offering; hosted SLA is slightly lower but we do offer enterprise SLA add-ons.

[13:25] Priya Nair: ok i'm going to show a slightly more complex flow: multi-turn extraction where the model first extracts conversation entities, then uses a function call to enrich from an internal CRM, and finally emits a routing decision. i'll step through the logs.

[13:45] [logs scrolling] Priya Nair: notice the KV cache entry for customer_id that gets reused for subsequent calls — that reduces tokens on follow-ups.

[14:05] Devon Park: can we persist KV cache between sessions? some customers want a short-lived context store.

[14:12] Priya Nair: yes, you can persist certain keys with TTL; Cache policies are configurable per-route.

[14:25] Michael Ortega: how do you handle schema evolution? our routing schema changes frequently during experiments.

[14:33] Alex Chen: Console supports versioned schemas and rollouts; you can pin routes to schema v1 or v2 and run canary traffic. we also emit diffs for failing examples so you can quickly update rules.

[14:55] Sara Li: pricing — curious for the bench/poc and for Dedicated.

[15:03] Alex Chen: for bench we'll provide a short eval package; pilot pricing depends on reserved capacity. i'll share a pricing spreadsheet but high-level: hosted per-token; Dedicated is monthly commit with discounts and reserved capacity.

[15:24] Priya Nair: another note — guardrails can be soft or hard. soft ones log and tag outputs, hard ones reject and trigger fallback. we suggest soft initially during canary.

[15:42] [15:42] Devon Park: ok can we see the code snippet for registering functions?

[15:47] Priya Nair: sure — here's a simple JSON: {"name": "route_ticket", "args_schema": {"type":"object","properties": {"order_id": {"type":"string"}, "suggested_routing": {"type":"string"}}}} and you wire a webhook URL. Redwood will validate the args against the schema before invocation.

[16:10] Michael Ortega: what about retries and idempotency? our routing API is idempotent but we need to avoid double actions.

[16:18] Priya Nair: we include an invocation id in headers and recommend idempotency keys on your side; Redwood can also dedupe near-term repeated calls within a short window.

[16:35] [demo: errors panel] Priya Nair: here's an example error where function_call was blocked by whitelist. Console captured the incident and suggested remediation.

[16:50] Anjali Rao: Data residency — will logs and cache stay in region? we operate in eu-west for EU customers.

[16:58] Jordan Kim: yes, region pinning is supported; for hosted we maintain EU regions, and for Private you can fully control region and storage.

[17:15] Michael Ortega: okay from here what's the minimal set of artifacts to run a bench?

[17:22] Priya Nair: sample corpus (500-1k emails), schema(s), desired canonical outputs, a list of APis/functions to call, and desired SLOs. with that we can run an eval and produce accuracy and latency reports.

[17:40] Devon Park: timeline and resource ask — how much lead time to get Dedicated set-up?

[17:46] Alex Chen: Dedicated typically 4–6 weeks after contract and infra details; Private on-prem can be longer depending on approvals. Hosted bench can start within a week.

[18:00] Sara Li: any integrations with their internal monitoring? we use Datadog.

[18:07] Jordan Kim: yes we stream metrics to Datadog, NewRelic, or push Prometheus metrics for Dedicated.

[18:20] [small laugh] Michael Ortega: ok budget question — what's an expected ballpark for a pilot?

[18:28] Alex Chen: pilots vary, but typical bench + pilot engagements are in the mid-five to low-six figure range depending on throughput and retention needs. we'll share a tailored quote.

[18:42] Priya Nair: one more console feature — regression alerts: tie prompt sets to production routes, and alert if extraction accuracy drops by X%. this helps catch silent regressions when you update model variants or quantization.

[19:00] Devon Park: about optimization — will Optimize recommend quantization profile per model automatically?

[19:08] Priya Nair: yes, it scores model/quantization combos on accuracy, latency, and cost using your prompts. you can preview tradeoffs before rollout.

[19:25] Michael Ortega: any notes about handling ambiguous inputs? sometimes emails lack order id; we need a robust fallback.

[19:33] Priya Nair: typical pattern: model returns 'order_id': null and suggested follow-up action; you can route to manual triage or a clarifying question flow. Console can flag ambiguous outputs for review.

[19:55] Alex Chen: ok let's cover next steps — i'll send security docs, Priya will scope the bench, and we'll schedule a follow-up with your infra/security folks.

[20:08] [multiple people agreeing]

[20:15] Michael Ortega: can you also include a sample contract language for data handling? that's handled by procurement.

[20:22] Alex Chen: yes we'll include standard DPA + data residency clauses and point to our enterprise terms.

[20:32] [demo wrap-up] Priya Nair: quick note — we also support prompt-level masking in logs so you won't store raw customer text unless allowed.

[20:45] Sara Li: good. any final technical caveats?

[20:50] Priya Nair: only that extraction accuracy can depend on prompt engineering; we'll run a guided prompt tuning as part of the bench to hit your targets.

[21:05] Devon Park: are there any open-source models you recommend for extraction vs. Redwood-curated ones?

[21:12] Priya Nair: for extraction we often recommend mid-sized models that optimize for token consistency; Redwood runs verified performance profiles — we'll suggest a few that match your latency/cost targets.

[21:30] Alex Chen: anything else from Gamma?

[21:33] Michael Ortega: no, that's it. thanks — this was helpful.

[21:40] Alex Chen: great, recap of action items — we'll send docs and scope. Priya will follow up on the bench plan. Devon will share sample data. Anjali we'll include security artifacts.

[21:55] Sara Li: thanks all.

[22:00] [meeting ends at ~15:48 PST; recording stops]

Notes on transcription quality: some minor mis-typings and speaker attribution errors in auto-transcript; representative of Fireflies output.
